body.target_estimand: The causal estimand is the exact unsmoothed clamp mean \(\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})=\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y\{d_{\delta_n}(A)\}]\).  It equals \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\) on the fixed-Hölder class by \(\texttt{prop:causal-bridge}\), and equals \(\theta_{\delta_n,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\) on the continuity-only class by \(\texttt{prop:continuity-causal-bridge}\), where in either case \(P\) is the observed margin.
body.estimand_functional: On the fixed-Hölder classes, \(\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})=\theta_{\delta_n}(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta_n\}]+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta_n)\mu_x^P(\delta_n)\), the observed and causal criteria are exactly equal for every \(n\), and their common order is \(r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta\).  On the continuity-only classes, \(\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})=\theta_{\delta_n,\mathrm{cont}}(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta_n\}]+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta_n)\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P(\delta_n)\), the corresponding observed and causal criteria are exactly equal for every \(n\), and their common order is \(s_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}\).

sampling_model.design: Independent random design with a fixed finite number of baseline strata, bounded outcomes, and author-imposed stratum probabilities at least \(p_{\min}\).
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), are sampled independently from either \(P\in\mathcal M\) for the fixed-Hölder result or \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) for the continuity-only result.
sampling_model.treatment: The observed-data functional is \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\) for the exact deterministic map \(d_{\delta_n}(a)=\max\{a,\delta_n\}\); it is neither smoothed nor replaced. On the declared full-data class, \(\texttt{prop:causal-bridge}\) identifies it with the causal clamp mean, and the onto observed-margin map makes the causal performance theorem an exact transport of the observed experiment.
sampling_model.overlap: Within each stratum, the conditional law of \(A\) has a Borel density satisfying the author-defined global measurable envelope \(c_-a^\kappa\leq\pi_x(a)\leq c_+a^\kappa\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The fixed-Hölder estimator uses empirical atom masses and a sample-split total-Gram local polynomial.  The continuity-only estimator uses the retained-course empirical mean, independent empirical joint atom masses, and the fixed regression fallback \(1/2\), with no local regression or propensity estimation.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Estimand: the threshold-LMTP mean; design class: the LMTP causal model with piecewise-smooth invertibility required only for continuous-exposure efficiency theory; moving-threshold status: no deterministic triangular-array frontier; delivered result: identification, together with non-pathwise differentiability of the continuous threshold example.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Díaz et al. supply the structural and identification template. The fixed-Hölder result adds the \(r_n\) observed-data frontier. The paper-defined full-data class, causal bridge, and onto observed-margin map then transport that frontier exactly; \(\texttt{thm:causal-frontier-lift}\) is this corollary, not an independently novel causal frontier. The continuity-only result adds the matched \(s_n\) frontier on a separate author-defined one-time specialization with finite strata, author-imposed positive stratum mass, bounded outcomes, polynomial thinning, and qualitative mean continuity. It is not labeled the published Díaz class. Its converse transfers to any broader compatible model containing this subclass, but its matched upper bound does not transfer to arbitrary longitudinal histories or treatment laws.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Estimand: a stochastic-shift effect-modifier target; design class: clipping is represented by a Radon--Nikodym comparison relative to an appropriate dominating measure, and the classification procedure targets the clipped pushforward law; moving-threshold status: no deterministic clamp sequence; delivered result: high-probability regularity and targeted-learning guarantees rather than minimax risk or uniformly honest expected length.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The fixed-Hölder and continuity-only observed-data frontier theorems record the proposal row: the exact deterministic clamp functionals; the author-defined polynomially thinned finite-stratum classes; every deterministic threshold sequence; and matched minimax risk plus uniformly honest expected length. The causal statements follow by the explicit bridge and onto full-data lift. Neither proposed estimator is attributed to current software.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Low proves a general lower-bound inequality for the expected length of a confidence interval that has prescribed coverage over a family of distributions and, as a corollary, shows that adaptation across derivative-smoothness density classes cannot improve the rate of interval length over minimax fixed-length intervals while retaining uniform coverage.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Low is the closest generic antecedent for the honest-inference obstruction when no common smoothness scale is available. The continuity-only theorem does not claim that generic obstruction as new: it derives for the exact clamp functional the explicit matched risk and honest-length rate \(n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}\), the elbow \(\delta_n\asymp n^{-1/[2(\kappa+1)]}\), and fixed-positive-threshold impossibility caused by the threshold-generated atom mass.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Estimand: a nonparametric regression functional such as a point value; design class: fixed-design local-polynomial formulations; moving-threshold status: no atom-weighted deterministic threshold sequence; delivered result: bias-aware honest confidence intervals with near-minimax expected length.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: \(\texttt{thm:honest-length}\) supplies the novel observed-data result for the exact clamp functional under polynomially thinned random design with singular-Gram fallback and every deterministic threshold sequence. \(\texttt{thm:causal-frontier-lift}\) transports that result to the paper-defined onto causal class; it is not positioned as an independent frontier beyond the observed theorem.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Estimand: an unweighted regression value at one fixed point; design class: a regularly varying degenerate random design; moving-threshold status: fixed point only; delivered result: the pointwise minimax regression rate determined by a bias-information fixed point.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The fixed-Hölder observed-data frontier combines the degenerate-design point rate with the clamp atom weight; the continuity-only theorem shows that removing every common modulus leaves the full atom mass as the irreducible term, with its exact moving-threshold scaling derived here.

A support-restricted stochastic threshold-response curve is root-\(n\) estimable and admits simultaneous efficient bands.
A doubly robust pseudo-outcome followed by local smoothing estimates the continuous-treatment dose-response at a point.

body.tldr: The primary novel result is the matched minimax-risk and uniformly honest expected-length frontier \(n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta\) for the observed-data clamp functional \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta_n\}]+\sum_xp_xq_x(\delta_n)\mu_x^P(\delta_n)\), where \(n h_n^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa\asymp1\). On the fixed finite-stratum Hölder model with the explicit treatment-assignment envelope \(c_-a^\kappa\leq\pi_x(a)\leq c_+a^\kappa\), a total-Gram-stabilized local polynomial, an atom-specific singular-design fallback, and same-class global-shift and localized-Bernoulli lower bounds yield the regular, critical, atom-dominated, and fixed-threshold regimes. A purpose-built full-data class satisfying simultaneous consistency, conditional exchangeability, and fiberwise structural-mean continuity maps onto the observed class; the causal bridge and this surjection make the causal risk and honest-length theorem an exact transport corollary of the observed frontier, not an independently novel frontier. On the continuity-only class, the matched rate is \(n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}\), with elbow \(\delta_n\asymp n^{-1/[2(\kappa+1)]}\) and fixed-positive-threshold impossibility. Low's 1997 general expected-length inequality and nonadaptation corollary are the closest generic honest-inference antecedent; the contribution here is the explicit threshold-atom scaling, matched moving-threshold risk and length, and causal transport for the exact unsmoothed clamp consumed by the official \(\texttt{lmtp}\) user-policy workflow.

project_justification.gap: Published LMTP identification covers the deterministic clamp, but its continuous-exposure efficiency theory does not provide rates for that non-pathwise-differentiable target. Low's 1997 theorem gives a general lower-bound inequality for the expected length of intervals honest over a distribution family and derives nonadaptation across derivative-smoothness density classes; it does not analyze a threshold-generated atom, polynomial thinning, or a deterministic moving threshold. McCoy et al. correctly accommodate clipping mass through an appropriate dominating measure and a classification estimator of the pushforward law, but their stochastic-shift effect-modifier target and high-probability regularity theory do not provide the deterministic moving-clamp minimax or uniformly honest expected-length frontier. Degenerate-design regression theory treats an unweighted fixed point, and existing bias-aware confidence-interval theory does not integrate this atom-weighted random-design problem.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied object is the observed functional \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\) induced by the exact unsmoothed clamp under polynomial generalized-propensity thinning, with a threshold that may follow any deterministic sequence and with inference honest across the transition where the shrinking atom becomes first-order. The associated causal statement is obtained by an explicit bridge and an onto full-data lift, so its scope is exactly the paper-defined structural class.
project_justification.fill: The known mixed-measure representation fixes the observed functional \(\theta_\delta(P)\); the explicit global measurable polynomial envelope defines the treatment-assignment class; the information-balance bandwidth and total-Gram lemma give an estimator on that class; two same-class experiments certify the minimax risk and confidence-length order; and the phase diagram converts those bounds into policy-facing regimes. The continuity-only theorem separately derives the atom-mass rate, elbow, and fixed-threshold impossibility rather than claiming the generic absence of honest adaptation as new. Finally, the causal bridge and surjective observed-margin construction transport the observed frontier exactly to the purpose-built full-data class for every \(n\).

body.related_work: Díaz, Williams, Hoffman, and Schenck identify threshold-LMTP means by sequential regression and show that the continuous threshold example is not pathwise differentiable. Their result supplies the identification template and standard causal premises, but it does not derive a deterministic moving-threshold minimax-risk or honest expected-length frontier. The present paper's full-data class additionally imposes fiberwise structural-mean continuity; together with consistency, conditional exchangeability, the continuous observed regression, and polynomial support, the proved causal bridge yields pointwise target equality. The separately proved observed-margin surjection then makes the causal frontier theorem a transport corollary of the novel observed-data frontier, not an independent causal-frontier discovery. Hoffman et al. repeat the piecewise-invertibility boundary in their applied tutorial, and Williams and Díaz document the \(\texttt{lmtp}\) user-policy workflow that consumes the exact unsmoothed policy specification. McCoy et al.'s MTP density ratio is a Radon--Nikodym derivative with respect to an appropriate dominating measure, expressly allowing clipping-induced boundary mass, and their classification estimator targets the clipped pushforward law directly. Their object is a stochastic-shift effect-modifier target, and their high-probability regularity theory does not deliver the minimax risk or uniformly honest expected-length frontier for the deterministic clamp with an arbitrary moving threshold. For generic honest nonparametric inference, Low (1997), \(\textit{On nonparametric confidence intervals}\), proves a lower-bound inequality for expected interval length under prescribed uniform coverage and derives as a corollary that adaptation across derivative-smoothness density classes cannot improve the interval-length rate over minimax fixed-length intervals while retaining uniform coverage. That antecedent already establishes the generic nonadaptation obstruction; the continuity-only theorem here instead derives the explicit matched clamp-functional rate \(n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}\), its moving-threshold elbow, and fixed-positive-threshold impossibility from the threshold-generated atom mass. Gaiffas derives the fixed-point regression rate and stabilized local polynomials under regularly varying degenerate random design. The global measurable envelope \(c_-a^\kappa\leq\pi_x(a)\leq c_+a^\kappa\) used here is an explicit treatment-assignment class, not a consequence attributed to regular variation; together with the exact conditional-density identity for every Borel set, it permits bounded measurable deviations from exact power behavior while retaining controlled boundary thinning. Armstrong and Kolesár construct bias-aware honest intervals for nonparametric regression under fixed-design formulations; the observed mixed functional \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\), vanishing random design, moving point, and singular-Gram expected-length integration are absent. Kennedy et al. motivate two-stage causal local regression, while Bonvini and Kennedy study dose-response rates under smooth positive conditional densities rather than polynomial thinning. Van der Laan, Zhang, and Gilbert obtain root-\(n\) bands for a support-restricted stochastic region-average threshold response, a different estimand not used as a comparator target. Shahu et al. extend simultaneous LMTP inference under piecewise invertibility rather than the continuous threshold map.
body.interpretation: The comparison between \(r_n\) and \(s_n\) isolates the statistical value of a common quantitative smoothness modulus.  Hölder control lets local information shrink the atom-regression error; qualitative continuity without a common modulus does not, because a fixed-height bump can be hidden in an arbitrarily narrow exposure window.  The continuity-only elbow \(\delta_n\asymp n^{-1/[2(\kappa+1)]}\) therefore marks when the whole atom mass becomes first-order.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The expected-length theorem requires the Hölder radius and thinning exponent to be declared. Adaptation to unknown \(\beta\) and \(\kappa\) is a separate ordered-modulus problem and may require a logarithmic payment. The accepted exact-modulus construction is retained only as a candidate handle: no theorem asserting its honesty, nondegeneracy, optimality, or a sharp asymptotic minimax constant is claimed. The higher-order literal-integral issue and the general exact-constant question remain open. The primary proved claims concern the sharp minimax risk and uniformly honest expected-length order uniformly over deterministic threshold sequences.
body.honest_scope: The paper fixes a finite number of strata, a bounded outcome, known smoothness radius on the Hölder class, and known thinning exponent. The novel matched minimax-risk and honest-length frontier is first proved for the observed-data functional. Its causal counterpart is not positioned as an independently novel frontier: it is transported exactly through the paper-defined full-data class, whose members have observed margins in the statistical class and satisfy simultaneous latent-response consistency, conditional exchangeability, and fiberwise structural-mean continuity on the threshold range. The causal bridge and the onto observed-margin proposition prove equality of targets, sampling experiments, minimax risks, and minimax honest expected lengths on precisely that class. These statements do not extend automatically to arbitrary longitudinal histories, arbitrary latent carriers outside the declared packages, or structural laws lacking the continuity premise. The continuity-only theorem is likewise confined to its separate author-defined class. Low's generic honest-inference nonadaptation result is prior art; the continuity-only contribution is the explicit threshold-atom rate \(n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}\), its elbow, and the fixed-positive-threshold impossibility. The paper proves no longitudinal recursion, no simultaneous band over a continuum of thresholds, and no claim about the validity or invalidity of McCoy et al.'s dominating-measure density-ratio estimator for their stochastic-shift effect-modifier target. Neither proposed estimator nor interval is claimed to be implemented in current \(\texttt{lmtp}\) software.
